CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly examination

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly exam. She reports doing well overall. She recently started working at a bakery this summer, which she has been enjoying, but she notes that she has been snacking frequently and consuming significantly more desserts than usual due to proximity to treats at work. She attributes her difficulty resisting temptation to the work environment. She reports that her blood sugars have been up and down, which she relates to her diet changes. She confirms she has been taking her diabetes medication as prescribed without any missed doses. Her blood pressure has remained good despite the fluctuating blood glucose levels. She denies any concerns with sleep, reporting she gets a full eight hours nightly. She denies any self-harm ideation or other concerning symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Otherwise unremarkable. No additional concerns beyond what has been discussed.

Type 2 diabetes
Hypertension
Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged from prior exams)
